title: Nipah virus outbreak in India: What do we know so far?

analysis.time: Published on 2026-09-30. The outbreak in Kerala was reported since last month, with the latest update on 4 October 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: India, specifically the southern state of Kerala. The affected population includes individuals who have been in contact with patients and the general public in the region.
analysis.event: A rare Nipah virus outbreak in Kerala, India, has been reported. The outbreak is being investigated by health authorities, and some schools have been closed as part of containment efforts.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Two deaths and four confirmed cases have been reported in Kerala since last month. The mortality rate for Nipah virus is between 40 and 75 percent, according to the WHO. Authorities have implemented mass testing and strict isolation measures to control the outbreak.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Authorities in Kerala are actively investigating the outbreak, conducting mass testing, and isolating individuals in contact with patients. The situation is under active monitoring, and the response is ongoing.

analysis.brief_en: A rare Nipah virus outbreak has been reported in Kerala, India, with two deaths and four confirmed cases since last month. The outbreak, which is being investigated by health authorities, has prompted the closure of some schools and the implementation of mass testing and strict isolation measures. The Nipah virus, which spreads from animals to humans and can also be transmitted directly between people, has a high mortality rate, ranging from 40 to 75 percent, according to the World Health Organization. The virus was first identified in 1998 in Malaysia and has since been recorded in Bangladesh and India, with both countries experiencing outbreaks since 2001. The outbreak in Kerala marks its fourth recorded spate of Nipah cases in five years. Health officials are working to contain the virus through testing and isolation, but the situation remains under active monitoring due to the potential for rapid spread and the lack of a vaccine.

title: New EU project aims to create first breathable treatment for Nipah virus - European Lung Foundation

analysis.time: The project was launched on 1 September 2026, with the publication date being 30 September 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The project, HENIPROTECT, involves 18 partners across eight countries and focuses on Nipah virus, which is prevalent in rural or farming areas of South-East Asia and Australia.
analysis.event: A new EU-funded project, HENIPROTECT, aims to develop the world’s first breathable treatment for Nipah virus infection. The European Lung Foundation (ELF) and the European Respiratory Society (ERS) are leading public-facing activities and scientific dissemination, respectively.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Nipah virus is classified as a ‘priority infectious disease’ by the WHO, with a high mortality rate of up to 75% in infected individuals. The project aims to address the lack of licensed preventions or treatments for this virus.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The project is in its initial phase, with plans to develop a new antibody treatment, test it in humans, and establish manufacturing standards. The European Lung Foundation will translate scientific results into lay language for public understanding.

analysis.brief_en: A new EU-funded project, HENIPROTECT, has launched to develop the world’s first breathable treatment for Nipah virus infection. The initiative, which began on 1 September 2026, involves 18 partners across eight countries and aims to address the lack of effective treatments for this highly dangerous virus. Nipah virus, carried by fruit bats in South-East Asia and Australia, can cause severe illness with a mortality rate of up to 75%. The European Lung Foundation (ELF) will lead public communication, translating scientific findings into lay language for patients and the general public. The project plans to test an antibody treatment through inhalation, develop a clinical trial, and create a blueprint for responding to future respiratory viral threats. The European Respiratory Society (ERS) will manage scientific dissemination, while advocacy efforts will be led through Lungs Europe. This project is part of the EU’s broader strategy to enhance health security and prepare for potential pandemics.
